newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Hungary flag snatched from consulate in Romania.
newsitem.headline: Hungary flag snatched from consulate in Romania.

text.p: The national flag was snatched on Friday from a Hungarian consulate two days after it was opened in the central city of Cluj despite fierce opposition from its Romanian nationalist mayor.

"This is theft," Cluj police chief Grigore Blaga said by telephone from the city, 400 km (250 miles) northwest of Bucharest. "The people who took the flag are being chased. We hope to give it back within an hour or two."
Police said they were chasing two unidentified men who put a ladder against the building housing the consulate, grabbed the red-white-green Hungarian flag and fled by car.

The consulate, shut by Communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu in 1988, was reopened by the two countries' foreign ministers on Wednesday to cheers from a crowd of several hundred. Many belonged to Romania's 1.6 million strong Hungarian community.

The ministers said the event in the heart of Transylvania, home to most ethnic Hungarians, marked a final break with communism and a big step in cementing improved relations after generations of mistrust between the two neighbours.
A diplomat at Hungary's embassy in Bucharest said the consul had watched helplessly as the flag was removed.

"The consul was in his office when a man in overalls climbed on a ladder to his window and took the flag," the diplomat said. "He asked him what he was doing and the man said he had been given orders to remove the flag."
Cluj mayor Gheorghe Funar had opposed the reopening of the consulate and vowed to impose a law introduced by the former leftist government banning the display of foreign flags on private buildings.
But Funar, who has twice run unsuccessfuly for Romanian president, said he was not involved in the incident.
"We have nothing to do with this. I have asked the central authorities to enforce the law after the Hungarian flag was illegally flown on the building," he told Reuters by telephone.
"These moves have offended the dignity of Romanians. Why are people pestering us with questions instead of asking the people who are breaking the laws?"
Funar this week fined the Hungarian Reformed Church which provided the apartment used for the consulate the equivalent of $4,000.

Its opening reflected improved ties after the neighbours signed a treaty last year to end centuries of mistrust. Romanian nationalists say Hungary wants to restore control over Transylvania, which it held under the Austro-Hungarian empire.

Funar won a new term as Cluj mayor in elections last year. He has antagonised ethnic Hungarians, who make up a quarter of the city's 300,000 population, by introducing curbs on their linguistic and cultural rights.
Romanian nationalists in the city of Tirgu Mures, south of Cluj, this week daubed Romanian flags over Hungarian-language inscriptions on bilingual signs.
